title: Sustainable Convergence and Polycrisis Resilience
subtitle: Integrating Economic Development, Environmental Sustainability and Systemic Risk Reduction
description: An H Heuristics flagship monograph—concept developed by Hunter Hughes—uniting Sustainable Convergence and Polycrisis Resilience into an integrated development…
contribution: Establishes the formal relationship between Sustainable Convergence and Polycrisis Resilience— concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics—demonstrating how economic catch-up, environmental decoupling, and systemic vulnerability reduction reinforce one another through 2100.
abstract: Sustainable Convergence and Polycrisis Resilience is a flagship publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).

keyFindings.title: Sustainable Convergence and Polycrisis Resilience are complementary halves of a unified development paradigm: economic catch-up in lower- and middle-income economies must occur alongside environmental sustainability and systemic vulnerability reduction.
Integrating both frameworks lifts the Resilient and Sustainable Global Development Index from 43.5 (2025) to 72.5 by 2050 and 92.0 by 2100, whereas Fossil-Lock-In Drift declines to 31.0.
Under Sustainable Convergence, Global South GDP per capita rises from 24.0% to 85.0% of the OECD frontier by 2100 while carbon-pollution intensity drops by 92.5% (100.0 → 7.5).
Systemic Risk & Vulnerability compresses from 65.0 (2025) to 10.0 by 2100 (-84.6%), delivering a 12.4x 25-year social benefit-cost ratio across the integrated portfolio.
